subject_id.description: A unique identifier for each participant in the study.
subject_id.clinical_usage: Used for data management, tracking individual patient progress over time, and linking various data points (e.g., lab results, imaging, clinical visits) to a single individual without revealing personal identity.

birthdate.description: The birth date of the study participant.
birthdate.clinical_usage: Essential for calculating age, which is a critical factor in risk stratification, interpreting age-dependent lab values, and determining appropriate treatment protocols.

sex.description: The biological sex of the study participant.
sex.clinical_usage: Used to interpret sex-specific reference ranges for laboratory tests, assess risk for sex-predominant diseases, and understand disease epidemiology.

Alcohol consumption.description: Patient-reported alcohol consumption status or amount.
Alcohol consumption.clinical_usage: Assesses a key lifestyle risk factor for numerous conditions, including liver disease (e.g., cirrhosis), cardiovascular diseases (cardiomyopathy, hypertension), pancreatitis, and certain cancers. It also informs medication choices and potential drug interactions.

Other addictive behaviors.description: Presence or history of addictive behaviors other than smoking or alcohol.
Other addictive behaviors.clinical_usage: Provides context for a patient's overall health, potential for non-adherence to treatment, and risk of specific complications (e.g., endocarditis in IV drug users). It is crucial for a comprehensive psychosocial assessment.

Smoking.description: The smoking status of the participant (e.g., current, former, never).
Smoking.clinical_usage: Identifies a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), various cancers, and poor wound healing. Smoking status influences treatment decisions and prognostic assessments.

ALAT.description: A blood test measuring the level of Alanine Aminotransferase, an enzyme primarily found in the liver.
ALAT.clinical_usage: A key biomarker for detecting and monitoring liver injury or inflammation (hepatitis). It is a standard component of a liver function panel (LFP).

Albumin to creatinine ratio.description: A ratio used to detect elevated protein in the urine (albuminuria), often an early sign of kidney damage.
Albumin to creatinine ratio.clinical_usage: A sensitive screening tool for detecting early kidney damage (nephropathy), particularly in patients with diabetes or hypertension. Elevated UACR is a marker for microalbuminuria or macroalbuminuria, indicating increased cardiovascular risk and progression of kidney disease.

ALP.description: A blood test measuring the level of Alkaline Phosphatase, an enzyme found throughout the body, particularly in the liver, bones, and digestive system.
ALP.clinical_usage: Used as part of a liver function panel to help diagnose cholestatic liver disease (problems with bile flow) or bone diseases with high bone turnover (e.g., Paget's disease, healing fractures).

ASAT.description: A blood test measuring the level of Aspartate Aminotransferase, an enzyme found in the liver, heart, and other muscles.
ASAT.clinical_usage: Used alongside ALT to diagnose and monitor liver damage. The AST/ALT ratio can provide clues to the cause of liver injury (e.g., a ratio >2:1 is suggestive of alcoholic liver disease). It can also be elevated in muscle injury or myocardial infarction.

Cholesterol total.description: The total amount of cholesterol in the blood, including both LDL and HDL cholesterol.
Cholesterol total.clinical_usage: A fundamental component of a lipid panel used for assessing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. High levels are a major risk factor for heart attack and stroke.

Cholesterol total.1.description: A repeated measurement of total cholesterol at a subsequent time point.
Cholesterol total.1.clinical_usage: Used to monitor the effectiveness of lifestyle modifications or lipid-lowering therapies (like statins) initiated after the baseline measurement.

Cholesterol total.2.description: A repeated measurement of total cholesterol at a subsequent time point.
Cholesterol total.2.clinical_usage: Provides a longer-term view of lipid control and patient adherence to treatment, allowing for further adjustments to therapy if goals are not met.

CPK.description: A blood test measuring the level of Creatine Phosphokinase, an enzyme found in the heart, brain, and skeletal muscles.
CPK.clinical_usage: Used to diagnose conditions causing muscle damage (myopathy), such as rhabdomyolysis, muscular dystrophy, and myocardial infarction (though more specific troponins are now preferred for MI). It is also monitored in patients on statin therapy who report muscle pain.

Creatinine.description: A blood test measuring the level of creatinine, a waste product from muscle metabolism, used to assess kidney function.
Creatinine.clinical_usage: A primary biomarker for assessing kidney function. Elevated serum creatinine levels suggest impaired kidney filtration, indicating acute kidney injury or chronic kidney disease.

Fasting glycemia.description: Blood glucose level measured after a period of fasting.
Fasting glycemia.clinical_usage: A key test for screening, diagnosing, and monitoring diabetes mellitus and prediabetes. It reflects the body's ability to manage glucose in the absence of food intake.

Fasting HbA1c.description: A blood test that measures the average blood sugar level over the past 2-3 months.
Fasting HbA1c.clinical_usage: A primary tool for diagnosing diabetes and prediabetes, and for monitoring long-term glycemic control in diabetic patients. It provides a more stable picture of glucose management than a single fasting glucose measurement.

Fasting insulinemia.description: Blood insulin level measured after a period of fasting.
Fasting insulinemia.clinical_usage: Used to assess insulin resistance, a condition where cells do not respond effectively to insulin. High fasting insulin levels, in the presence of normal or high glucose, are a hallmark of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.

GFR.description: An estimate of how well the kidneys are filtering waste from the blood, typically calculated from serum creatinine levels.
GFR.clinical_usage: The most important measure of overall kidney function. It is used to stage chronic kidney disease (CKD), guide drug dosing for medications cleared by the kidneys, and determine the need for dialysis.

Haematocrit.description: The proportion of red blood cells in the blood, expressed as a percentage.
Haematocrit.clinical_usage: A standard part of a complete blood count (CBC). It is used to diagnose and monitor anemia (low hematocrit) or polycythemia (high hematocrit). It also provides information about hydration status.

HDLc.description: The level of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol in the blood, often referred to as 'good' cholesterol.
HDLc.clinical_usage: Part of a lipid panel to assess cardiovascular risk. Higher levels of HDL-C are generally associated with a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

HDLc.1.description: A repeated measurement of HDL cholesterol at a subsequent time point.
HDLc.1.clinical_usage: Monitors the response to interventions aimed at increasing HDL-C, such as exercise, smoking cessation, or certain medications (e.g., fibrates, niacin).

HDLc.2.description: A repeated measurement of HDL cholesterol at a subsequent time point.
HDLc.2.clinical_usage: Assesses long-term changes in HDL-C levels and the sustained effect of lifestyle or pharmacological interventions.

hsTnT.description: A blood test measuring the level of Troponin T, a protein specific to heart muscle, used to detect cardiac injury.
hsTnT.clinical_usage: A critical biomarker for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (heart attack). Its high sensitivity allows for earlier detection of cardiac injury. Chronically elevated levels can also indicate chronic cardiac stress or damage and carry prognostic value in conditions like heart failure.

LDH.description: A blood test measuring the level of Lactate Dehydrogenase, an enzyme involved in energy production that is found in many body tissues.
LDH.clinical_usage: A non-specific marker of tissue damage. While historically used for diagnosing myocardial infarction, it has been replaced by more specific troponins. It is still used to monitor tissue breakdown in conditions like hemolysis, certain cancers, and severe infections.

LDLc.description: The level of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol in the blood, often referred to as 'bad' cholesterol.
LDLc.clinical_usage: A primary target of therapy for preventing cardiovascular disease. Lowering LDL-C with statins and other medications is a cornerstone of ASCVD risk reduction.

LDLc.1.description: A repeated measurement of LDL cholesterol at a subsequent time point.
LDLc.1.clinical_usage: Crucial for assessing the efficacy of lipid-lowering therapy and determining if treatment goals have been reached or if medication needs to be adjusted.

LDLc.2.description: A repeated measurement of LDL cholesterol at a subsequent time point.
LDLc.2.clinical_usage: Evaluates long-term adherence and response to lipid-lowering strategies, ensuring sustained control of cardiovascular risk.

NT-proBNP.description: A blood test measuring the level of NT-proBNP, a hormone released in response to heart muscle stretch, used as a marker for heart failure.
NT-proBNP.clinical_usage: A key biomarker for the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of heart failure. High levels strongly suggest the presence of heart failure, and changes in levels can indicate response to treatment.

Platelets.description: The number of platelets (thrombocytes) in a volume of blood.
Platelets.clinical_usage: Measured as part of a complete blood count (CBC). Low platelet counts (thrombocytopenia) increase bleeding risk, while high counts (thrombocytosis) can increase clotting risk.

Triglycerides.description: The level of triglycerides, a type of fat (lipid), in the blood.
Triglycerides.clinical_usage: Measured as part of a lipid panel. High levels (hypertriglyceridemia) are associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and, at very high levels, can cause pancreatitis.

Triglycerides.1.description: A repeated measurement of triglycerides at a subsequent time point.
Triglycerides.1.clinical_usage: Monitors the effectiveness of lifestyle changes (diet, exercise) and medications (e.g., fibrates, statins, omega-3 fatty acids) aimed at lowering triglyceride levels.

Triglycerides.2.description: A repeated measurement of triglycerides at a subsequent time point.
Triglycerides.2.clinical_usage: Assesses long-term control of hypertriglyceridemia and the sustained impact of therapeutic interventions.

us-CRP.description: A blood test measuring C-Reactive Protein, a marker of inflammation in the body. The 'us' or 'hs' prefix indicates a high-sensitivity test.
us-CRP.clinical_usage: Used as a biomarker to assess the risk of future cardiovascular events. Persistently elevated hs-CRP levels indicate chronic low-grade inflammation, which is implicated in the development of atherosclerosis.

Gamma-GT.description: A blood test measuring the level of Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase, an enzyme found mainly in the liver.
Gamma-GT.clinical_usage: A sensitive marker for liver and biliary tract disease. It is often elevated in cases of alcohol abuse and can be used to monitor abstinence. It is typically interpreted alongside other liver function tests like ALP and ALT.

Fat mass.description: The total mass of fat in the body, typically measured by methods like DEXA or bioimpedance.
Fat mass.clinical_usage: Used to assess obesity and body composition beyond simple BMI. High fat mass is a risk factor for metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease.

Lean mass.description: The total mass of the body minus the fat mass (includes muscle, bone, organs).
Lean mass.clinical_usage: Assesses nutritional status and muscle mass. Low lean mass (sarcopenia) is associated with frailty, poor physical function, and increased mortality, especially in older adults and chronically ill patients.

Skeletal muscle index.description: A measure of muscle mass relative to height, often calculated as appendicular skeletal muscle mass divided by height squared.
Skeletal muscle index.clinical_usage: A key diagnostic criterion for sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss). A low SMI indicates reduced muscle mass relative to body size, which is a predictor of functional decline and adverse health outcomes.

Total mass.description: The total mass of the participant's body.
Total mass.clinical_usage: A fundamental measurement used to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI), dose medications, and track weight changes over time, which is critical in managing conditions like heart failure and malnutrition.

A.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the peak velocity of late diastolic blood flow across the mitral valve, corresponding to atrial contraction.
A.clinical_usage: Used in the assessment of left ventricular diastolic function. An abnormally high or low A-wave velocity, especially in relation to the E-wave, helps to grade the severity of diastolic dysfunction.

COsimpson.description: Echocardiographic estimation of cardiac output (volume of blood pumped per minute) using Simpson's biplane method.
COsimpson.clinical_usage: A fundamental measure of overall cardiac performance. It is used to assess hemodynamic status in patients with heart failure, shock, and valvular heart disease. Low cardiac output indicates poor heart function.

Dt.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the time from the peak of the E-wave to its extrapolation to the baseline, reflecting the rate of pressure equalization between the left atrium and ventricle.
Dt.clinical_usage: A key parameter for assessing left ventricular diastolic function and estimating LV filling pressures. A shortened DT (<160 ms) suggests high left atrial pressure and restrictive filling, which is a sign of advanced diastolic dysfunction.

E.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the peak velocity of early diastolic blood flow across the mitral valve.
E.clinical_usage: A primary component in the assessment of left ventricular diastolic function. Its velocity reflects the pressure gradient between the left atrium and left ventricle in early diastole.

EA.description: The ratio of early (E) to late (A) diastolic mitral inflow velocities, a key parameter in assessing diastolic function.
EA.clinical_usage: A fundamental parameter for evaluating left ventricular diastolic function. A normal ratio is typically between 1 and 2. A low ratio (<0.8) suggests impaired relaxation (Grade 1 diastolic dysfunction), while a high ratio (>2) suggests restrictive filling (Grade 3 diastolic dysfunction).

EDPWT.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the thickness of the left ventricular posterior wall at the end of diastole.
EDPWT.clinical_usage: Used to assess for left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), a thickening of the heart muscle often caused by chronic hypertension or aortic stenosis. Increased thickness is a marker of adverse cardiac remodeling.

EDSWT.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the thickness of the interventricular septum at the end of diastole.
EDSWT.clinical_usage: Used, along with posterior wall thickness, to diagnose and quantify left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). Asymmetric septal hypertrophy is a hallmark of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

EFsimpson.description: Echocardiographic estimation of the left ventricular ejection fraction using Simpson's biplane method, a measure of systolic function.
EFsimpson.clinical_usage: The most common and important measure of left ventricular systolic function. It is used to diagnose and classify heart failure (e.g., HFrEF vs. HFpEF), guide therapy, and determine prognosis. A normal EF is typically >50-55%.

LA-LS-conduit.standard_name: Left Atrial Longitudinal Strain - Conduit Phase
LA-LS-conduit.description: A measure of the left atrium's function as a passive conduit for blood flow from the pulmonary veins to the left ventricle during early diastole.
LA-LS-conduit.clinical_usage: An advanced measure of left atrial function. Impaired conduit function reflects LA stiffness and is associated with advanced left ventricular diastolic dysfunction and conditions like atrial fibrillation.

LA-LS-contract.standard_name: Left Atrial Longitudinal Strain - Contraction Phase
LA-LS-contract.description: A measure of the left atrium's contractile function (booster pump) during late diastole.
LA-LS-contract.clinical_usage: An advanced measure of left atrial contractile function. Reduced contraction strain indicates a weaker 'atrial kick,' which can impair ventricular filling and is often seen in atrial fibrillation or advanced diastolic dysfunction.

LA-LS-res.standard_name: Left Atrial Longitudinal Strain - Reservoir Phase
LA-LS-res.description: A measure of the left atrium's ability to store blood from the pulmonary veins during ventricular systole.
LA-LS-res.clinical_usage: A key advanced measure of left atrial function, reflecting LA compliance and filling. Reduced reservoir strain is an early and sensitive marker of left atrial dysfunction, often preceding LA enlargement, and is a strong predictor of adverse cardiovascular events like atrial fibrillation and heart failure.

latE'.standard_name: Lateral Mitral Annular Early Diastolic Velocity (e')
latE'.description: Tissue Doppler measurement of the early diastolic velocity of the lateral mitral annulus, reflecting myocardial relaxation.
latE'.clinical_usage: A measure of myocardial relaxation. It is used in the E/e' ratio to estimate left ventricular filling pressures. A low lateral e' velocity (<10 cm/s) is a sign of impaired relaxation and diastolic dysfunction.

LAV_ES_al.standard_name: Left Atrial Volume End-Systole by Area-Length
LAV_ES_al.description: Estimation of the left atrial volume at the end of ventricular systole (maximum LA volume) using the area-length method.
LAV_ES_al.clinical_usage: Used to assess left atrial size. Left atrial enlargement is a marker of chronic volume or pressure overload, commonly due to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, and is a significant risk factor for atrial fibrillation and stroke.

LAV_ES_simpson.standard_name: Left Atrial Volume End-Systole by Simpson's Method
LAV_ES_simpson.description: Estimation of the left atrial volume at the end of ventricular systole (maximum LA volume) using Simpson's biplane method.
LAV_ES_simpson.clinical_usage: The preferred method for quantifying left atrial size. When indexed to body surface area (LAVi), it is a powerful prognostic marker for a wide range of cardiovascular diseases.

LVEDD.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the internal diameter of the left ventricle at the end of diastole.
LVEDD.clinical_usage: A simple, one-dimensional measure of left ventricular size. An increased LVEDD indicates left ventricular dilation, which can be seen in conditions like dilated cardiomyopathy or severe aortic regurgitation.

LVEDV.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the volume of blood in the left ventricle at the end of diastole.
LVEDV.clinical_usage: A key measure of left ventricular size and preload. It is used to calculate stroke volume and ejection fraction. Increased LVEDV signifies volume overload or ventricular dilation.

LVESV.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the volume of blood remaining in the left ventricle at the end of systole.
LVESV.clinical_usage: A sensitive marker of left ventricular systolic function and contractility. An increased LVESV indicates impaired emptying of the ventricle and is a strong predictor of adverse outcomes in heart failure.

LVOT.description: Echocardiographic measurement of the diameter of the left ventricular outflow tract.
LVOT.clinical_usage: An essential measurement used to calculate the cross-sectional area of the LVOT, which is then used in the continuity equation to calculate stroke volume, cardiac output, and aortic valve area.

LVOT VTI.standard_name: Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Velocity Time Integral
LVOT VTI.description: Doppler measurement of the integral of blood flow velocity over time in the LVOT, used to calculate stroke volume.
LVOT VTI.clinical_usage: A crucial component for calculating stroke volume (Stroke Volume = LVOT Area x LVOT VTI) and cardiac output. It is a robust measure of forward blood flow from the left ventricle.

RV-GLS.description: A measure of the deformation (shortening) of the right ventricular myocardium along its long axis, indicating RV systolic function.
RV-GLS.clinical_usage: A sensitive and quantitative measure of right ventricular systolic function. It can detect RV dysfunction earlier than traditional measures like TAPSE or FAC and is an important prognostic marker in pulmonary hypertension, heart failure, and congenital heart disease.

septE'.standard_name: Septal Mitral Annular Early Diastolic Velocity (e')
septE'.description: Tissue Doppler measurement of the early diastolic velocity of the septal mitral annulus, reflecting myocardial relaxation.
septE'.clinical_usage: A measure of myocardial relaxation. A low septal e' velocity (<7 cm/s) indicates impaired relaxation. It is used in the E/e' ratio (often an average of septal and lateral e') to estimate LV filling pressures and diagnose diastolic dysfunction.

TR Vmax.description: The maximum velocity of the tricuspid regurgitant jet, measured by Doppler echocardiography, used to estimate pulmonary artery pressure.
TR Vmax.clinical_usage: A critical measurement used to estimate the systolic pressure in the pulmonary artery. Using the simplified Bernoulli equation (4 x V²), this velocity is converted to a pressure gradient between the right ventricle and right atrium, which is a key component in diagnosing and assessing the severity of pulmonary hypertension.

GCS_ap.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) in the circumferential direction at the apical level of the left ventricle.
GCS_ap.clinical_usage: Part of a detailed analysis of left ventricular mechanics. Regional variations in strain can indicate specific patterns of myocardial damage, such as in certain types of cardiomyopathy or ischemia.

GCS_bas.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) in the circumferential direction at the basal level of the left ventricle.
GCS_bas.clinical_usage: Used in advanced analysis of LV function. A base-to-apex gradient of strain is normal; alterations in this pattern can be indicative of disease.

GCS_mid.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) in the circumferential direction at the mid-ventricular level of the left ventricle.
GCS_mid.clinical_usage: Contributes to the overall assessment of LV mechanics and helps identify regional wall motion abnormalities that may not be apparent by visual assessment.

GLS-2CH.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) along the long axis of the left ventricle, calculated from the apical 2-chamber view.
GLS-2CH.clinical_usage: A component of the overall LV Global Longitudinal Strain (GLS) calculation. It specifically assesses the function of the anterior and inferior walls of the left ventricle.

GLS-3CH.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) along the long axis of the left ventricle, calculated from the apical 3-chamber view.
GLS-3CH.clinical_usage: A component of the overall LV Global Longitudinal Strain (GLS) calculation. It specifically assesses the function of the anteroseptal and inferolateral (posterior) walls of the left ventricle.

GLS-4CH.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) along the long axis of the left ventricle, calculated from the apical 4-chamber view.
GLS-4CH.clinical_usage: A component of the overall LV Global Longitudinal Strain (GLS) calculation. It specifically assesses the function of the septal and lateral walls of the left ventricle.

COVID19 results.description: The result of a test for SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19).
COVID19 results.clinical_usage: Used to diagnose an active or recent COVID-19 infection, which has known cardiovascular and systemic implications. This information is important for clinical context, as the infection can cause myocarditis, thrombosis, and other complications.

Basal Insulin.description: Indicates whether the patient is using a long-acting (basal) insulin.
Basal Insulin.clinical_usage: A key component of many insulin regimens for type 1 and advanced type 2 diabetes. It is used to control blood glucose levels between meals and overnight.

Type 2 diabetes diagnosis - Year.description: The calendar year in which the patient was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes.
Type 2 diabetes diagnosis - Year.clinical_usage: Used to calculate the duration of diabetes, which is a critical factor in assessing the risk of developing long-term diabetic complications such as retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy.

Sleep Apnea Syndrome - History.description: Indicates whether the patient has a history of diagnosed Sleep Apnea Syndrome.
Sleep Apnea Syndrome - History.clinical_usage: Identifies a comorbidity that is a significant independent risk factor for hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Management of OSA is important for cardiovascular health.

Calcium Channel Blockers.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking Calcium Channel Blocker medication.
Calcium Channel Blockers.clinical_usage: These drugs are widely used to treat hypertension, angina pectoris, and certain cardiac arrhythmias by relaxing blood vessels and/or reducing heart rate and contractility.

Dyspnea (NYHA).description: Classification of the severity of dyspnea (shortness of breath) according to the New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification system.
Dyspnea (NYHA).clinical_usage: A cornerstone in the assessment and staging of heart failure. The NYHA class is used to guide therapy, monitor patient status, and provide prognostic information.

Metformin (biguanides).description: Indicates whether the patient is taking Metformin or another biguanide medication.
Metformin (biguanides).clinical_usage: The first-line oral medication for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. It primarily works by decreasing glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity.

Beta-blockers.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking Beta-blocker medication.
Beta-blockers.clinical_usage: A cornerstone therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), coronary artery disease (post-MI), and hypertension. They work by blocking the effects of adrenaline, thereby reducing heart rate, blood pressure, and cardiac workload.

Sulfonamides.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Sulfonylurea medication for diabetes. (Note: 'Sulfonamides' can also refer to antibiotics, but in a diabetes/cardiac context, it typically means sulfonylureas).
Sulfonamides.clinical_usage: Used to treat type 2 diabetes, often as a second-line agent after metformin. Their use has declined due to risks of hypoglycemia and weight gain compared to newer agents.

Diastolic blood pressure.description: The pressure in the arteries when the heart rests between beats.
Diastolic blood pressure.clinical_usage: A vital sign used to diagnose and monitor hypertension. Both systolic and diastolic pressures are important for assessing cardiovascular risk.

Weight.description: The measured body weight of the participant.
Weight.clinical_usage: A fundamental anthropometric measurement used to calculate BMI, dose medications, and monitor for fluid retention (a key sign of worsening heart failure) or weight loss (a sign of cachexia or poor nutrition).

GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a GLP-1 Receptor Agonist medication.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.clinical_usage: Used to treat type 2 diabetes. They work by increasing insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon, slowing gastric emptying, and promoting satiety. Many have proven cardiovascular and weight loss benefits.

Fibrates.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Fibrate medication, typically for managing cholesterol.
Fibrates.clinical_usage: Used primarily to lower high triglyceride levels. They may also modestly increase HDL-C. Their role in primary cardiovascular prevention is debated, but they are important for managing severe hypertriglyceridemia to prevent pancreatitis.

Loop Diuretics.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Loop Diuretic medication.
Loop Diuretics.clinical_usage: A cornerstone for managing fluid overload and relieving symptoms (like dyspnea and edema) in patients with acute or chronic heart failure. Also used for edema from other causes, such as liver or kidney disease.

Potassium Sparing Diuretics.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Potassium-Sparing Diuretic medication.
Potassium Sparing Diuretics.clinical_usage: Spironolactone and eplerenone are also Aldosterone Receptor Antagonists and are key therapies in HFrEF and post-MI care. Amiloride and triamterene are weaker diuretics used to counteract potassium loss from other diuretics.

Diabetic feet - History.description: Indicates whether the patient has a history of diabetic foot problems, such as ulcers or neuropathy.
Diabetic feet - History.clinical_usage: Identifies patients at high risk for future foot problems. A positive history necessitates regular, specialized foot examinations and patient education to prevent severe complications like amputation.

Ankle swelling.description: Presence of swelling (edema) in the ankles.
Ankle swelling.clinical_usage: A classic sign of fluid retention, commonly seen in congestive heart failure. It can also be caused by kidney disease, liver disease, venous insufficiency, or as a side effect of certain medications (e.g., some calcium channel blockers).

Other origin.description: A categorical variable indicating an origin or cause not otherwise specified. Context is needed for a more specific definition.
Other origin.clinical_usage: Used in data collection to classify etiologies that do not fit into predefined categories, ensuring comprehensive data capture. For example, 'dyspnea of other origin' could mean it's from anemia rather than heart failure.

Microalbuminuria.description: Indicates the presence of small amounts of albumin in the urine, an early sign of kidney disease.
Microalbuminuria.clinical_usage: A key screening finding for diabetic nephropathy and hypertensive kidney disease. Its presence indicates an increased risk for progression to overt kidney disease and is also a strong independent predictor of cardiovascular events.

DPP-4 Inhibitors.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a DPP-4 Inhibitor medication.
DPP-4 Inhibitors.clinical_usage: Oral medications used to treat type 2 diabetes. They work by increasing the levels of incretin hormones, which in turn increases insulin secretion and decreases glucagon levels in a glucose-dependent manner.

Hip.description: The measured circumference of the hips at their widest point.
Hip.clinical_usage: Used in conjunction with waist circumference to calculate the waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), an indicator of body fat distribution. A high WHR is associated with increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disease.

LV_peak_systolic_rad_strain.standard_name: Left Ventricular Peak Systolic Radial Strain
LV_peak_systolic_rad_strain.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (thickening) in the radial direction during systole.
LV_peak_systolic_rad_strain.clinical_usage: A component of multi-dimensional strain analysis that reflects myocardial contraction. While less robust and reproducible than longitudinal strain, it provides complementary information about LV mechanics.

Statins.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Statin medication.
Statins.clinical_usage: The first-line and most important class of drugs for lowering LDL ('bad') cholesterol. They are fundamental to the primary and secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).

SGLT-2 Inhibitors.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking an SGLT-2 Inhibitor medication.
SGLT-2 Inhibitors.clinical_usage: Oral medications for type 2 diabetes that work by causing the kidneys to excrete excess glucose in the urine. They have been shown to have significant benefits in reducing cardiovascular events and hospitalizations for heart failure, and in slowing the progression of chronic kidney disease, independent of their glucose-lowering effect.

Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.description: Presence of attacks of severe shortness of breath and coughing that generally occur at night.
Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.clinical_usage: A highly specific symptom of congestive heart failure. It is caused by the reabsorption of fluid from the lower extremities back into the circulation when supine, which overloads the failing heart.

LV_peak_systolic_circ_strain.standard_name: Left Ventricular Peak Systolic Circumferential Strain
LV_peak_systolic_circ_strain.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) in the circumferential direction during systole.
LV_peak_systolic_circ_strain.clinical_usage: A sensitive measure of LV systolic function that complements longitudinal strain. It is particularly useful for assessing conditions that disproportionately affect the subepicardial layers of the myocardium.

Orthopnea.description: Presence of shortness of breath that occurs when lying flat.
Orthopnea.clinical_usage: A classic symptom of congestive heart failure, caused by the redistribution of fluid to the central circulation when in a supine position, which increases pulmonary congestion.

CARDIATEAM group.description: The assigned group for the participant within the CARDIATEAM study (e.g., intervention or control).
CARDIATEAM group.clinical_usage: Used for statistical analysis to compare the effects of an intervention against a control or another intervention. This is fundamental to determining the efficacy and safety of the treatment being studied.

Glitazones.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Glitazone (TZD) medication.
Glitazones.clinical_usage: Oral medications for type 2 diabetes that work by improving insulin sensitivity in muscle and fat tissue. Their use is limited due to side effects, including weight gain, fluid retention (which can worsen heart failure), and an increased risk of bone fractures.

Reduced exercise tolerance.description: Patient-reported reduction in the ability to perform physical exercise.
Reduced exercise tolerance.clinical_usage: A common and often early symptom of many chronic conditions, particularly heart failure and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It is a key component of the NYHA functional classification.

Systolic blood pressure.description: The pressure in the arteries during the contraction of the heart muscle.
Systolic blood pressure.clinical_usage: A critical vital sign for diagnosing and managing hypertension. Elevated systolic blood pressure is a major risk factor for stroke, heart attack, and heart failure.

Retinopathy.description: Indicates the presence or history of diabetic retinopathy.
Retinopathy.clinical_usage: A marker of end-organ damage from long-standing or poorly controlled diabetes. Its presence often correlates with other microvascular complications like nephropathy and neuropathy.

Thiazides.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Thiazide Diuretic medication.
Thiazides.clinical_usage: A first-line class of medications for the treatment of hypertension. They work by inhibiting sodium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubules of the kidneys, leading to salt and water excretion.

Type 2 diabetes.description: Indicates whether the patient has a diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes.
Type 2 diabetes.clinical_usage: Identifies a major comorbidity that is a primary risk factor for cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and other systemic complications. The diagnosis dictates a wide range of management strategies.

Geographic\u00a0origin.description: The geographic origin or ethnicity of the participant.

Waist.description: The measured circumference of the waist.
Waist.clinical_usage: A key anthropometric measurement for assessing central (abdominal) obesity. Increased waist circumference is a strong predictor of metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, and cardiovascular disease, independent of BMI.

Alpha-glucosidase Inhibitors.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking an Alpha-glucosidase Inhibitor medication.
Alpha-glucosidase Inhibitors.clinical_usage: Oral medications for type 2 diabetes that work by slowing the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the small intestine, thereby reducing post-meal blood glucose spikes. They are less commonly used due to modest efficacy and gastrointestinal side effects.

B0 VISIT DATE.description: The date of the participant's baseline (B0) visit for the study.
B0 VISIT DATE.clinical_usage: Serves as the primary time point (T=0) against which all subsequent follow-up data are compared. It is essential for calculating time-to-event outcomes and tracking changes over the duration of the study.

ACEIs/ARBs.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking an Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) Inhibitor or an Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB).
ACEIs/ARBs.clinical_usage: These are first-line therapies for hypertension, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and chronic kidney disease (especially with proteinuria). They work by blocking the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), leading to vasodilation and reduced cardiac remodeling.

Angina pectoris.description: Presence or history of angina pectoris (chest pain due to reduced blood flow to the heart).
Angina pectoris.clinical_usage: Identifies a patient with symptomatic coronary artery disease. The characteristics of the angina (e.g., stable vs. unstable) are critical for risk stratification and determining the urgency of further investigation and treatment.

Aldosterone Receptor Antagonists.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking an Aldosterone Receptor Antagonist (e.g., Spironolactone, Eplerenone).
Aldosterone Receptor Antagonists.clinical_usage: A key evidence-based therapy for patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and for certain patients after a myocardial infarction to reduce mortality and morbidity. They are also used for resistant hypertension.

COPD.description: Indicates whether the patient has a diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).
COPD.clinical_usage: Identifies a major comorbidity that frequently coexists with cardiovascular disease. COPD can cause or exacerbate heart failure (especially right-sided), and its symptoms (like dyspnea) can overlap, complicating diagnosis. Medication choices for heart disease (e.g., beta-blockers) must be made carefully in patients with COPD.

Diabetic neuropathy.description: Indicates whether the patient has a diagnosis of diabetic neuropathy.
Diabetic neuropathy.clinical_usage: A common and debilitating complication of diabetes. Its presence is a marker of long-standing disease and is a major risk factor for diabetic foot ulcers and amputations. It can also affect autonomic nerves, leading to cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and genitourinary problems.

Palpitations.description: Patient-reported presence of heart palpitations (a feeling of a fast-beating, fluttering, or pounding heart).
Palpitations.clinical_usage: A common symptom that can be benign (e.g., caused by anxiety or caffeine) or a sign of a significant cardiac arrhythmia, such as atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, or ventricular tachycardia. It often prompts further investigation with an ECG or Holter monitor.

Height.description: The measured body height of the participant.
Height.clinical_usage: A fundamental anthropometric measurement used to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI) and Body Surface Area (BSA), the latter of which is crucial for indexing echocardiographic measurements (e.g., LV mass, LA volume) to body size.

Insulin Pump.description: Indicates whether the patient uses an insulin pump for diabetes management.
Insulin Pump.clinical_usage: Represents an advanced and intensive method of insulin therapy, most commonly used by patients with type 1 diabetes or insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes, to achieve tighter glycemic control.

LV_peak_systolic_long_strain.standard_name: Left Ventricular Peak Systolic Longitudinal Strain
LV_peak_systolic_long_strain.description: A measure of myocardial deformation (shortening) along the long axis of the left ventricle during systole.
LV_peak_systolic_long_strain.clinical_usage: A highly sensitive and reproducible measure of LV systolic function. It can detect subtle myocardial dysfunction even when the ejection fraction is normal (e.g., in HFpEF, chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity, or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy). An impaired GLS (less negative value) is a powerful predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes.

Glinides.description: Indicates whether the patient is taking a Glinide medication for diabetes.
Glinides.clinical_usage: Oral medications for type 2 diabetes that act as short-acting insulin secretagogues. They are taken before meals to reduce postprandial glucose excursions. Their use is limited due to the need for frequent dosing and risk of hypoglycemia.

Heart rate.description: The number of heartbeats per minute.
Heart rate.clinical_usage: A fundamental vital sign. It is used to assess cardiac rhythm, hemodynamic stability, and response to exercise or stress. In chronic conditions like heart failure, a lower resting heart rate is often a therapeutic goal.
